definition: Money earned from products sold. Computed from order_items as quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount_pct / 100). Excludes orders whose status is 'cancelled' or 'returned'. Shipping fees are NOT revenue.
sql: SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount_pct / 100.0)) ... FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.status NOT IN ('cancelled', 'returned')

definition: Profit = revenue minus product cost, where cost = quantity * products.cost_price. Margin % = profit / revenue * 100. Same status exclusions as revenue.
sql: SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount_pct / 100.0) - oi.quantity * p.cost_price) AS profit

definition: Revenue divided by the number of distinct orders, using only orders that are not cancelled or returned.
The company's fiscal year runs from 1 April to 31 March and is named after the year it ENDS in. FY2026 = 1 Apr 2025 to 31 Mar 2026. Fiscal quarters: Q1 Apr-Jun, Q2 Jul-Sep, Q3 Oct-Dec, Q4 Jan-Mar.
sql: EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date + INTERVAL '9 months') AS fiscal_year

definition: A customer who placed at least one order that was not cancelled in the last 90 days (relative to CURRENT_DATE).
sql: o.status <> 'cancelled' AND o.order_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '90 days'

definition: A customer who has ordered before but whose most recent order is more than 180 days ago.
A customer with two or more orders that were not cancelled.
Customers counted by customers.signup_date falling in the period asked about (not by first order date).
An inventory row where quantity_on_hand is below reorder_level. Out of stock means quantity_on_hand = 0. Stock is per warehouse; total stock of a product = SUM over warehouses.
Days between placing and receiving an order: delivered_date - order_date::date. Only for orders with delivered_date not null. Processing time = shipped_date - order_date::date.
categories is a two-level tree. Products link to sub-categories. To report by top-level category (Electronics, Fashion, Books, ...) join categories twice: sub.parent_category_id = top.category_id.
sql: JOIN categories sub ON sub.category_id = p.category_id JOIN categories top ON top.category_id = sub.parent_category_id

definition: Rank by average reviews.rating, but only products with at least 10 reviews so a single 5-star review does not win.
sql: GROUP BY p.product_id HAVING COUNT(r.review_id) >= 10 ORDER BY AVG(r.rating) DESC

definition: Share of orders with status 'cancelled' (or 'returned') out of all orders in the period, as a percentage.
Orders that are not finished yet: status in ('pending', 'processing', 'shipped').
Orders handled by sales employees are linked by orders.handled_by = employees.employee_id. handled_by is NULL for self-service web orders.
sql: JOIN employees e ON e.employee_id = o.handled_by

definition: Market means the customer's country (customers.country), not the warehouse country. India-specific payment methods: 'upi' and 'cod' (cash on delivery).

term: Last month / this month / last N days
definition: Relative periods use CURRENT_DATE. 'Last month' = the previous full calendar month. 'This year' = calendar year unless the user says fiscal year.
sql: o.order_date >= date_trunc('month', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '1 month' AND o.order_date < date_trunc('month', CURRENT_DATE)

definition: employees.manager_id is a self-reference. Use a self-join for direct reports and WITH RECURSIVE for the full chain under someone.
sql: JOIN employees m ON m.employee_id = e.manager_id
